To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel AFG3L mutation was identified in a Czech patient with slowly progressive ataxia, and that this mutation is associated with a phenotype distinct from that of the previously described SCA28 cases.
we have identified the first AFG3L mutation in a patient with ataxia in the Czech Republic and that the mutation is a frameshift mutation in the AFGL3 gene.
we identified a novel frameshift mutation in the AFGL32 gene in a patient with spinocerebellar disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first AFG3LZ frameshift mutation reported in the Czech Republic and the first report on a SCA28 patient with mild Parkinsonian features.
the first AFG3L3L2 frameshift mutation in a patient with SCA28.
a novel frameshift mutation in the AFG2L3 gene in a patient with SCA28.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SCA28 is a rare disease in the Czech population.
the AFG33L2 mutation is associated with the phenotype of the proband, but the exact mechanism remains unclear.
the AFG33L2 frameshift mutation is not the only cause of the disease in this family and that it is not a common cause of SCA28.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AFG33L2 gene should be screened for mutations in all ataxic patients.

the SCA28 phenotype is highly heterogeneous and that the frameshift mutation c1958dupT is a novel AFG3L mutation associated with a late-onset, slowly progressive form of ataxic disorder with mild parkinsonism and polyneuropathic signs.
the frameshift mutation c.[1958dupT] in AFG3L1 causes a novel phenotype of slowly progressive ataxia with mild Parkinsonian features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCA28 should be included in the differential diagnosis of ataxia with onset in adulthood.
AFG3LZ2 frameshift mutations are rare and that the phenotypic spectrum of SCA28 is broader than previously thought.
SCA28 should be considered in the differential diagnosis of ataxia with a late onset, especially if accompanied by mild Parkinsonian features.
